stories.headline: Young humpback whale off Maui may be orphaned calf
stories.summary: Researchers think the whale seen swimming frantically off Maui may be the calf of a humpback that washed ashore on Molokaʻi, and its survival chances are low.
stories.text: A young humpback whale was spotted off Maui on Tuesday swimming frantically, and Marine Mammal researchers believe it is the orphaned calf of a humpback that washed ashore on Molokaʻi three weeks ago. If so, its chances of survival are low because baby whales rely on mother's milk during the first year of life. Sadly, researchers say if it is the baby calf, there's little anyone can do and the likely long-term scenario is that it will become food for sharks. More observation is needed to determine age and identity.

stories.headline: Maui News to be sold to local nonprofit
stories.summary: Ogden Newspapers has agreed to sell the Maui News to the nonprofit Maui Nui Media and Creativity Collaborative, with financial terms undisclosed.
stories.text: Maui's oldest newspaper is getting new local ownership. The Maui News announced it has reached an agreement to be sold by Ogden Newspapers to the nonprofit Maui Nui Media and Creativity Collaborative. According to the newspaper, the new owners plan to preserve the Maui news local journalism mission, while expanding community-focused reporting and supporting the next generation of Maui journalists and storytellers. Financial terms of the sale were not disclosed. The transition would move ownership of the more than century-old newspaper from a mainland media company to a Maui-based nonprofit organization.

stories.headline: Police investigate $81,000 luxury retail theft
stories.summary: Police arrested an 18-year-old visitor and detained a 15-year-old after three suspects took more than $81,000 in goods from two luxury stores, while a third juvenile fled.
stories.text: Police are investigating an organized retail theft that targeted luxury stores in Wailua Tuesday night. Investigators say three male suspects stole five luxury handbags, a wallet, and a polo shirt worth a combined estimated value of more than $81,000 from two retailers Officers arrested an 18-year-old visitor from Miami and detained a 15-year-old from Lahaina, while a third juvenile suspect fled the area. A search warrant executed Wednesday recovered five luxury handbags, $378 in cash and nearly one gram of suspected cocaine. The 18-year-old The man posted $6,000 bail and was released, while the juvenile was released to his parents as the investigation continues. Anyone with information is asked to contact Maui police.

stories.headline: RIMPAC exercises sink two decommissioned ships off Kauai
stories.summary: Navies from seven countries held live-fire drills at RIMPAC, sinking the USS Mobile Bay and USS Peleliu off Kauai's northern coast after rough weather canceled beach landings.
stories.text: Although the story is under-reported, there is a war wrapping up this week on Hawaiian soil. The annual war games exercise known as RIMPAC. Rough weather canceled beach landings, but warships and aircraft from the U.S., Australia, Italy, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, and Spain conducted live-fire exercises at sea, including unleashing weapons on the decommissioned USS Mobile Bay on July 12 and the USS Peleliu on July 17, sinking them off the northern coast of Kauai.

stories.headline: Planning Commission backs Pahia Train Depot rezoning
stories.summary: The Maui Planning Commission unanimously recommended rezoning the Pahia Train Depot property from urban reserve to business country town.
stories.text: The Maui Planning Commission unanimously recommended approval of a zoning change for the historic Pahia Train Depot property on Baldwin Avenue to change the property's zoning from urban reserve to business country town, bringing the zoning into alignment with the site's current commercial uses.

stories.headline: Free screening of Maʻalaea Bay restoration documentary
stories.summary: A free screening of a documentary on restoring Maʻalaea Bay's reefs is set for August 13 at 6 p.m. at the Sphere, followed by a panel discussion.
stories.text: A long-time dream of Ocean Center General Manager Tupani Vori has been to bring the Dead Sea of a once-magnificent Ma'alaiā Bay back to life. And it may just become a dream come true. Ma'alaiā Bay was once celebrated for its vibrant coral reefs. Now only 5% remains. But restoration is in sight. A free public screening of a new documentary, Ma'alaiʻa, Taste for Regeneration, is happening at the Sphere on Thursday, August 13th, 2026 at 6 p.m. Doors open at 5.30. There will be a panel discussion after the film.

stories.headline: Marine council expands reef monitoring with temperature loggers
stories.summary: The Maui Nui Marine Resource Council is installing underwater temperature loggers with Aqualink and Malamakai Foundation and will present 10 years of water quality data on August 25.
stories.text: The Maui Nui Marine Resource Council is expanding efforts to track the health of Maui's reefs With a new partnership with Aqualink and Malamakai Foundation to install long-term underwater temperature loggers on mooring buoys across Maui Nui, providing real-time data on changing ocean conditions as a strong El Nino continues. The Council also announced a free virtual presentation on August 25 highlighting 10 years of water quality monitoring, including Findings from more than 5,500 water samples collected around Maui. The report is expected to identify long-term effects on the island's coastal waters and coral reefs.

stories.headline: Sammy Hagar's airport restaurant donates profits to children's charities
stories.summary: Sammy Hagar has given all of his profits from Sammy's Beach Bar and Grill at Kahului Airport to children's charities, including the Keiki Aloha Fund, since 2008.
stories.text: Rock legend Sammy Hagar's restaurant inside Kahului Airport has quietly been giving back to Hawaiʻi's children for nearly two decades. Since opening Sammy's Beach Bar and Grill in 2008, Hagar has donated 100% of his own profits from the restaurant to children's charities through the Hagar Family Foundation. Those funds have supported organizations across Maui, including the Keiki Aloha Fund, which helps families travel off-island when children need specialized medical care. Hagar sold his Maui home in 2017, but his restaurant continues to generate donations that support local keiki every day. So if you're killing time before your flight, it's not a bad place to stop.

stories.headline: Kilauea's 52nd lava fountain episode ends
stories.summary: Episode 52 of lava fountaining at Kilauea's Halemaumau crater ended after more than seven hours, sending ash as high as 19,000 feet, and volcanologists predict another episode.
stories.text: Madame Pelly is in the news once again as episode 52 of Lava Fountaining at Kilauea's Hale Maʻu Crater ended earlier today after more than seven hours of shooting molten rock 500 feet into the air. It sent volcanic ash as high as 19,000 feet. Volcanologists predict another episode is on the way.

stories.headline: High surf continues to hit Maui shores
stories.summary: Though the High Surf Advisory expired, large waves still wrap around West Maui near oceanfront businesses as a south swell builds and another east swell from Hurricane Genevieve is expected.
stories.text: The high surf advisory for east-facing shores expired earlier this evening, but powerful surf is still making an impact across Maui, with large waves wrapping around west Maui, surging onto the shoreline and pushing water near oceanfront hotels and businesses. A separate south swell has begun building. Surf from former tropical depression Fausto will continue The county is expected to fade, but another east swell is expected to follow from Hurricane Genevieve.

stories.headline: County to remove four speed tables on West Kuiaha Road
stories.summary: Mayor Richard Bissen says the County will begin removing four speed tables on West Kuiaha Road the week of August 17th after resident complaints, with a community meeting set for August 26th.
stories.text: Finally, some action regarding those annoying speed bumps in the road. After months of complaints from Haikū residents, Mayor Richard Bissen says the county will begin removing four speed tables on West Kuiaha Road starting the week of August 17th. The speed tables were originally installed to slow traffic, but residents raised concerns about vehicle damage, drainage, and the quantity of them. The county is also reviewing future speed table requests and will host a community meeting on the issue. That meeting will be held August 26th at 5.30 p.m. at the Haikū Community Center.

stories.headline: 12 states oppose Paramount-Warner merger; Ellison reassures staff
stories.summary: Attorneys General in 12 states oppose the Paramount-Warner Brothers Discovery merger, and David Ellison told employees he believes there are no legal obstacles.
stories.text: Maui-affiliated media mogul has just hit a bit of a speed bump himself. Attorneys General in 12 states are opposing the Paramount Warner Brothers discovery merger on antitrust grounds, saying it will create a monopoly that will dominate TV news, basic cable, and movie theaters. Notably, Hawaiʻi is not one of them. David Ellison, son of Larry Ellison, who owns 98% of the island of Lānaʻi, just wrote a letter to his employees telling them not to worry about it, that it may take a while to work through 12 lawsuits, but he believes there are no legal obstacles and that the merger will eventually go through.

stories.headline: Utility pole fire causes South Kihei outage
stories.summary: A utility pole caught fire near Kaiola Street, causing outages from North Kihei to Uwapo Road and Kihei Villages, and the cause has not been announced.
stories.text: A power outage affected parts of South Kīhei this morning after a utility pole caught fire near Kaiola Street. Maui Fire Department crews responded around 8 a.m. while Hawaiian Electric worked to restore service. Residents reported outages from North Kīhei to Uopo Road and Kīhei villages, with power returning to some neighborhoods later in the morning. The cause of the poll fire has not yet been announced.

stories.headline: PETA seeks criminal investigation over calf death at Makawao Stampede
stories.summary: PETA gave video to the Maui Prosecutor's Office that it says shows a calf dying during the Makawao Stampede and has requested charges, while organizers have not responded.
stories.text: The animal rights organization People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, or PETA, is calling for a criminal investigation after a calf died during the Mokawa Stampede this year. The group says it submitted video to the Maui Prosecutors Office that appears to show a calf being roped around the neck and swung around a pole before going limp, and The board of agriculture is urging prosecutors to determine whether Hawaiʻi's animal cruelty laws were violated. PETA says it has requested charges against those responsible. Organizers of the Makua Stampede have not yet publicly responded to the allegations.

stories.headline: New rule restricts moving plant material between Maui and Lānaʻi
stories.summary: The Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity approved a rule, effective today, restricting transport of certain plant materials between Maui and Lānaʻi to stop the coconut rhinoceros beetle.
stories.text: Beetles, keep out. The Hawaiʻi Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity has approved a rule to help prevent the spread of the coconut rhinoceros beetle to Maui and Lānaʻi. Effective today, July 29, the rule restricts transporting live plants with attached organic material, untreated mulch, compost, wood chips, plant propagation media, and coconut fruit between the two islands. Certain items, including bare root plants, treated materials, seeds, cut flowers, most fruits and vegetables, lumber and sterile tissue-cultured plants, are exempt unless, of course, you spot a beetle trying to hitch a ride.

stories.headline: Molokai farmers work together amid barge delays
stories.summary: Molokai farmers say they are collaborating to keep produce available after missed Young Brothers barge deliveries, and hope for more local agriculture.
stories.text: Recent shipping delays and new plant import restrictions are highlighting the importance of growing food close to home. Molokaʻi farmers say they're working together to keep fresh produce available after missed Young Brothers barge deliveries left grocery stores' shelves bare, and biosecurity rules continue to limit the import of many plants to protect the islands from invasive pests. Growers hope the challenges will encourage greater food security by expanding local agriculture

The company says locally grown watermelons, sweet onions, and new Maui Harvest cantaloupes are now available at retailers across Hawaiʻi, Including Costco Maui with 100% Maui grown coffee expected to arrive in Costco stores soon through a partnership with Maui Coffee Roasters.

stories.headline: Haleakalā silverswords reach week seven of bloom
stories.summary: The endemic Haleakalā silversword is in week seven of flowering, with stalks measuring 62 and 72 inches tall.
stories.text: Visitors to the summit of Haleakalā National Park have a rare opportunity to witness one of the park's most iconic native plants in bloom. The endemic Haleakalā Silver Sword has now reached week seven of its flowering cycle, with one flower stock measuring 62 inches tall and another growing to 72 inches. Silver Swords bloom just once in their lifetime And before producing seeds and dying back. Visitors heading to the summit this summer may even catch the plant's floral scent drifting on the breeze.

stories.headline: Council committee hears update on Kīpuola Kauhale tiny homes

stories.text: On Saturday, America will celebrate its 250th birthday. And even though we are the 50th star on the flag, it's not nearly as big a deal here in Hawaiʻi as it is on the continent. Other than the Makawao Stampede and some fireworks, there's not a lot going on on Maui. The state of Hawaiʻi set up an America 250 commission with no state funding and they raised hardly any money to fund the celebration. The commission did purchase and hand out 130 custom America 250 flags, but that's about it. The lack of interest is kind of understandable, since Captain Cook hadn't even arrived here until 1778, when the Revolutionary War in the American colonies was still going on. And, of course, there was the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom in 1893. It does make one wonder, though, during the Age of Conquest, if America did not annex Hawaiʻi in 1897, what other nation's birthday would we be celebrating?
